bug_semantics: Bitcoinrb's experimental SPV RPC HTTP server (lib/bitcoin/rpc/http_server.rb) parses a POST JSON body into method/params and dispatches with Ruby Object#send(command, *args) while including RequestHandler. There is no allowlist that command is an intended RPC method, so a client can invoke Kernel#eval / Kernel#system (and any other reachable method) with attacker-controlled arguments. The published PoC POSTs {"method":"eval","params":["File.write(\"/tmp/pwned\",\"owned\")"]} to the EventMachine listener (binds 0.0.0.0:8332 by default). The sink is the unvalidated send of JSON method plus splatted JSON params; CWE-77 as reviewed by GHSA-q66h-m87m-j2q6. Affected gem range is < 1.12.0; 070327133a2a3e5a6d265b2d82f06f9414c01e74 added SUPPORTED_COMMANDS and rejects unknown methods before send.
flaw_origin: The command-injection sink is send(command, *args) fed by parse_json_params, which first appears in 3a777e737b0e4aeaf703757d2dc0f2969df08d8a (2017-10-17, 'Implement getblockheader RPC'). That commit changed process_http_request from send(command) with only JSON method to command, args = parse_json_params; send(command, *args), because getblockheader(hash, verbose) needed arguments. The parent 456b95475796ccf2ab5467d06915b9cfbb97662d still has send(command) only — eval/system with attacker params cannot run there. The previous day's bc61832d7aaab6d9d04415af692cd2a5a6dac65e first added the RPC server and unvalidated send(command) without args; git log -L tracks the send line through that commit, but that form is not the GHSA mechanism (no params forwarding). Later 770dd4ce0b6980157354e95d232e9cf733532a02 and 4733643bd72fda6e2f9e5549ed1900964cbe87e8 only moved the same send(command, *args) into EM.defer/rescue; they are not BICs.

Vulnerable mechanism at v1.11.0 (e46ca90f40226a02487d9d3c399534de78752d4c) lib/bitcoin/rpc/http_server.rb: command, args = parse_json_params then send(command, *args).to_json with no method allowlist; HttpServer includes RequestHandler and Kernel methods remain reachable via send.

reasoning: GHSA-q66h-m87m-j2q6 is a real, vendor-acknowledged RCE in the experimental bitcoinrb RPC HTTP server: JSON method/params are passed to Ruby send with no RPC-method allowlist, so eval/system execute attacker strings. GitHub lists no CVE; CVE.org has no record; the GHSA is not withdrawn. The disclosed sink is specifically send(command, *args) after parse_json_params. That pair is first written in 3a777e737b0e4aeaf703757d2dc0f2969df08d8a; the immediate parent still has send(command) only, so the advisory PoC cannot fire there. git log -L shows an earlier 2017-10-16 commit bc61832d7aaab6d9d04415af692cd2a5a6dac65e introduced unvalidated send(command) when the RPC server was created, but that is a weaker unsafe-dispatch precursor, not the command-injection mechanism (no args forwarding). Later EM.defer/rescue edits are moves of the same *args send and are not BICs. The whitelist fix 070327133a2a3e5a6d265b2d82f06f9414c01e74 lands in v1.12.0 and is absent from v1.11.0, matching the advisory range. AI judgment is from the BIC commit object only: human author/committer azuchi@haw.co.jp in 2017, no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailers, not a bot. Therefore NOT_AI.
